title: NREL / NLR Developer APIs (alt fuel stations, utility rates, solar resource, PVWatts)
agency: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), U.S. Department of Energy
questions: how many public EV charging stations are in each state
DC fast chargers by network in a state
average residential electricity rate for a location
expected output of a rooftop solar system

key_only: 1,000 requests an hour instead of DEMO_KEY's 30 an hour and 50 a day per IP address (live headers have shown as few as 10 an hour)

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser after replacing {API_KEY} with your free api.data.gov key (or DEMO_KEY for a few requests), save the JSON under the name shown and upload it. Stations without a key: https://afdc.energy.gov/stations (Station Locator) > filter > Download Results (CSV) or https://afdc.energy.gov/data_download; PVWatts: https://pvwatts.nlr.gov (monthly results > Download CSV).

cache.why: Station data change daily; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: Data produced for the U.S. Department of Energy and published openly through the developer network and the Alternative Fuels Data Center; cite the laboratory and the API, and do not imply endorsement.

citation: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), U.S. Department of Energy, {dataset}, developer.nlr.gov API, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Count stations or charging ports? One station can have many EV ports (ev_level2_evse_num, ev_dc_fast_num).
Open public stations only (pass status=E, access=public) or every station? Without them the API returns all statuses (open, planned, temporarily unavailable) and private stations too.
